`z.record` now drops any entry whose key schema outputs exactly `"__proto__"`. It raises no issue and writes no value, so the result keeps `Object.prototype`. The record tests pass, including a new one I added.

The change is a one-line check in the general (non-literal-key) branch of the record parser in `packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts`. Because it sits in core, it covers `parse`, `safeParse` and the async paths, in both classic and mini. It sits before the value schema runs, so it also covers async value schemas. The existing check on a raw `"__proto__"` input key is untouched.

The new test in `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/record.test.ts` parses `{"__PROTO__": …, "KEY": …}` through `z.string().toLowerCase()`, sync and with an async refinement on the value. It checks that the prototype is `Object.prototype`, that `result.a` is undefined, and that only `key` is an own property. That also shows normal key normalization still works.

I only tested the `.toLowerCase()` case. The other key mechanisms you listed (`.trim()`, `.normalize()`, `.transform()`, `z.preprocess`, `.pipe()`, codecs) go through the same check on the key schema's output, but I didn't run them individually. I also didn't run the mini API or the rest of the suite.
